## Citation

Joshi, M., Pero, S.C., Durocher, Y., Sun, Y., Shukla, G., Murphy, C., Barrantes-Reynolds, R., Bernard, C., Welch, G., & Krag, D.N. (2026). Phase 1, Open-Label Clinical Trial to Treat Stage IV Cancer Patients Harboring Multiple Patient-Specific Mutated Cell Surface Proteins with Chimeric Antibodies. Presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting, May 29-June 2, 2026, Chicago, Illinois.

## Abstract

This phase 1 clinical trial evaluates the safety and efficacy of personalized chimeric antibody therapy in stage IV cancer patients with multiple tumor-specific mutations. The approach combines neoantigen identification, antibody engineering, and personalized immunotherapy.

## Study Design

- **Phase:** Phase 1, open-label
- **Population:** Stage IV cancer patients with multiple tumor-specific mutations
- **Intervention:** Patient-specific chimeric antibodies targeting mutated cell surface proteins
- **Primary Outcomes:** Safety, tolerability, dose escalation
- **Secondary Outcomes:** Clinical response, immunogenicity

## Key Features

- Personalized medicine approach tailored to individual tumor mutations
- Chimeric antibody engineering for enhanced tumor targeting
- Multiple patient-specific mutations targeted simultaneously
- Represents innovative approach to immunotherapy

## Role

As a co-author, I contributed bioinformatics and genomic analysis of tumor-specific mutations and neoantigen identification.
